title: Release of Retainage on Construction Loans
content:
Retainage withheld from the builder on Construction Loans is held until the project is complete and is then released in full.

## Term

Retainage is released in one amount equal to the retainage held after the final inspection finds the project complete and final lien waivers from the builder and every subcontractor and supplier are received, within the product's retainage release period in calendar days after the completed date; it is disbursed to the builder and becomes principal. Retainage is never released early in part, and is released before conversion so that the permanent loan repays the full construction balance.

## Restated

- **Amount:** the whole retainage held on the loan, in one amount; never a part of it ahead of completion.
- **Conditions:** (i) the final inspection has found the project complete, and (ii) final lien waivers have been received from the builder and from every subcontractor and supplier.
- **Time:** within the product's retainage release period, counted in calendar days after the completed date.
- **Payee and effect:** the released amount is paid to the builder; the retainage held falls by that amount and the construction principal owed rises by it.
- **Relation to conversion:** release comes before conversion, so the permanent loan repays the full construction balance.

## Conditions combined

| Final inspection has found the project complete | Final lien waivers received from the builder and every subcontractor and supplier | Retainage released |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes, the full amount held, within the release period after the completed date |
| Yes | No | No |
| No | Yes | No |
| No | No | No |

## Points of judgement

- *Can part of the retainage be paid to the builder as stages finish?* No. Retainage is never released early in part.
- *Where does released retainage go?* To the builder, and it becomes principal on the construction loan.
